newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Robotics sees product demand growing.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Robotics sees product demand growing.

text.p: U.S. Robotics Corp, which reported record fiscal 1996 fourth quarter earnings and revenues, said Monday it expects demand for all of its product lines to continue to grow substantially in fiscal 1997.

U.S. Robotics reported earnings for its fiscal 1996 fourth quarter rose to $67.4 million, or $0.71 a share, from $34.2 million, or $0.37, in the same period a year ago. Fiscal 1996 results exclude a one-time charge related to the company's acquisition of Scorpio Communications Ltd.
Fiscal 1996 fourth quarter earnings were in line with a First Call consensus estimate of $0.71.

"The company expects demand for all of its product lines to continue to grow substantially in the 1997 fiscal year as world-wide requirements increase for highly integrated, cost-effective, end-to-end information access solutions," said John McCartney, U.S. Robotics executive vice president and chief operating officer.

The company also expects that its sales of network systems products will continue over time to grow at a more rapid rate than sales of its PC related products (desktop and PC Card products), it said in a statement.

Sales growth is expected to be driven by increases in unit sales of existing products and by new products, which will be offset in part by anticipated future reductions in the average selling prices of existing products, the company said.

McCartney also said that the company would continue to invest in new technologies such as x2 (its 56 kilobit per second modem), wireless, switching and broadband access, including digital subscriber line technologies, during the coming year. "We feel it is essential to the ongoing health of the company to continue our investments in technology development," he said.

U.S. Robotics expects to continue its strategy to build market share. The company said it intends to continue to build its sales force, with particular focus on expanding sales of its network systems products domestically and internationally.

Depending on the growth in revenues achieved, these investments, coupled with expenses related to the launch of the company's new x2 products, may cause selling and marketing expenses in the first half of fiscal 1997 to represent a higher percentage of total sales than in recent quarters.

U.S. Robotics said its ability to achieve its revenue and profitability objectives in fiscal 1997 and market acceptance of x2 and other new products will depend on many factors beyond the company's control. These include the timing introduced by the company and its competitors and the extent to which the company is successful in implementing its on-going strategy of continuously improving the performance/cost characteristics of its products through improved designs and manufacturing efficiencies. Other factors include rapid changes in technologies and standards relating to information access and telecommunications.
U.S. Robotics supplies products and systems that provide access to information.
